content.text: The clause matches the preferred position exactly — New York law, exclusive New York County courts, no arbitration.

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: The clause sits at our preferred position: New York law governs (with CISG expressly disclaimed), and the state and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and waiver of forum objections. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the document, so no foreign-seat arbitration risk. The carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief in another court is mutual and standard, and the pre-filing executive escalation in 28.3 is a fifteen-business-day good-faith step that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-preserving filings — neither is a deviation. No redline needed.
